doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Forgotten mouthpiece, and hearing Charlie Parker with Hot Lips Page
summary: A mouthpiece story and Pete hearing a young Charlie Parker in Hot Lips Page's group at the Sherman Hotel.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You know I think Conte told me a story about you were playing in Chicago or something and you forgot your mouthpiece. And he had to come up and deliver it to you or something.

Yeah. I think I remember that. I says I didn’t have my mouthpiece. And you can’t play like you play without — it’s like wearing someone else’s gloves or shoes, something’s wrong with them. Especially when, obviously like I have no calluses on my hand so I can’t play the guitar. It’s about that simple. I didn’t even worry about anything, to be honest with you, but I remember when I was with Tommy Dorsey at the Sherman Hotel, Hot Lips Page had a band, a small group, they played in between with Tommy and then we’d do the set and then Hot Lips Page would play. And he had a saxophone player that was playing weird. He was going for [scats] he was trying for runs, trying to make certain runs. It was fine — and the rhythm section — and it was Charlie Parker. It was Bird. Unbelievable. I said wow, that guy’s going for runs. But I didn’t understand. You know because to be honest with you, too —I was, technically — too young, and doing things that way. But I wasn’t saying anything. What a difference.
Yeah, yeah, you’ve got to say something.
